title: Leveraging National Science Data Fabric Services to Train Data Scientists
problem: Data scientists lack practical knowledge and hands-on experience in managing, analyzing, and visualizing scientific datasets exceeding 100TB across heterogeneous storage and computing environments. The technical challenge is integrating data storage, streaming, and visualization capabilities into cohesive workflows for large-scale scientific data analysis.
motivation: Scientific research increasingly demands processing datasets at petabyte scales, requiring accessible platforms and training to empower researchers to leverage modern data infrastructure effectively.
method: The tutorial teaches NSDF services as an integrated platform for data-intensive computing, combining public and private storage, streaming solutions, and visualization dashboards. Participants build modular workflows through hands-on exercises using Earth science data, learning intermediate techniques for constructing analysis pipelines and advanced methods for high-resolution data visualization and management.
key_novelty: NSDF provides a unified, production-ready platform that abstracts the complexity of petabyte-scale data management, allowing researchers to construct scalable scientific workflows without managing underlying infrastructure.
contributions: Interactive tutorial demonstrating comprehensive NSDF capabilities for managing datasets exceeding 100TB
Hands-on exercises teaching modular workflow construction for data-intensive Earth science applications
Advanced techniques for visualization and analysis of massive high-resolution scientific datasets
Practical strategies for integrating NSDF services into research workflows and enabling collaborative scientific discovery

metrics.other: not provided - educational tutorial without empirical benchmarking

limitations: Not discussed - the paper is a tutorial documentation and does not address technical limitations or comparative evaluation of NSDF.
primary_theme: Educational platform for data-intensive scientific computing at scale
